skill.name: security-engineering
skill.description: Security architecture guidance for authentication, authorization, threat modeling, compliance controls, security testing, secrets management, and incident response planning.
skill.summary: Design and review application security controls with structured engineering guidance.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

content.value_statement: Security work often spans architecture, identity, compliance, testing, and response planning. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured security engineering guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains defense in depth and zero trust architecture patterns.
Guides OAuth 2.0, OIDC, session management, and MFA choices.
Compares RBAC, ABAC, and policy as code approaches.
Summarizes OWASP Top 10 mitigation strategies and security testing methods.
Outlines secrets management, compliance controls, and incident response phases.
limitations: Does not include runnable scanners, scripts, or automated enforcement.
Does not replace expert review for regulated systems or live incidents.
References supplemental files that are not included in this package.
Provides general patterns, not organization-specific control mappings.

use_cases.title: Design Authentication Controls
use_cases.description: Select OAuth, OIDC, session, and MFA patterns for a product architecture review.

use_cases.title: Prepare A Threat Model
use_cases.description: Structure security questions around access control, data protection, and common application risks.

use_cases.title: Map Compliance Work
use_cases.description: Identify common control areas for SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GDPR, or ISO 27001 planning.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Security Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security-engineering skill to review this design. Focus on identity, data protection, logging, and missing controls.

prompt_templates.title: Choose An Authorization Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security-engineering skill to compare RBAC, ABAC, and policy as code for this product. Recommend a practical model.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Secure Development Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security-engineering skill to create a release checklist for OWASP risks, testing, dependencies, and secrets management.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Incident Response Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security-engineering skill to assess this incident response plan. Identify gaps in detection, containment, recovery, and lessons learned.

output_examples.input: Review our login and session design for a web application.
output_examples.output: A concise review covering token lifetime, secure cookies, session timeout, MFA options, rate limiting, and logout behavior.

output_examples.input: Help us plan security testing before launch.
output_examples.output: A prioritized testing plan with SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, severity gates, and ownership recommendations.

output_examples.input: Compare compliance control areas for a payment feature.
output_examples.output: A plain-language control map covering access, encryption, logging, incident response, vendor review, and training needs.

best_practices: Provide system context, data sensitivity, and deployment model before requesting security guidance.
Ask for tradeoffs when choosing between identity, authorization, and monitoring controls.
Validate final recommendations with your security team and regulatory obligations.
anti_patterns: Do not treat general control guidance as a complete compliance audit.
Do not paste live secrets, private keys, or production credentials into prompts.
Do not use the skill to justify unsafe exceptions without compensating controls.

faq.question: Does this skill run security scans?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and review structure, but it does not run tools or scan systems.

faq.question: Can it help with OAuth and OIDC?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common grant types, token practices, sessions, and MFA considerations.

faq.question: Does it support compliance planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It summarizes common control areas for SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GDPR, and ISO 27001.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it for code review?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide security review questions for authentication, authorization, secrets, and OWASP risks.

faq.question: Does it include incident response guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines preparation, detection, containment, eradication, recovery, and lessons learned.

faq.question: Is it enough for regulated production systems?
faq.answer: No. Use it as planning support and validate decisions with qualified security and compliance reviewers.
